reasons: The lake identity identifies the case as State of Arizona v. Ian Mitcham in the Arizona Supreme Court, decided 2024.
The lake citation display and selected official citation are 559 P.3d 1099, matching the asserted reporter citation and year.
residual_risks: The opinion text header shows docket No. CR-23-0236-PR while the content/lake docket field shows CR-23-0238-PR, but docket was not part of this assertion.

reasons: The opinion discusses both independent-source and inevitable-discovery exceptions at paragraphs 34-36.
The holding applies the inevitable-discovery exception to DNA evidence, so placement under an Inevitable Discovery & Independent Source home is supported.
The decision date is 2024-12-17, supporting a recent-development role.
residual_risks: The role should not be read to mean the court applied independent source as the dispositive exception.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If displayed with a short role note, say this is a recent inevitable-discovery DNA decision that distinguishes independent source.

defect.evidence_quote: In sum, the inevitable discovery exception applies here, and the trial court therefore erred by suppressing Mitcham’s DNA profile.
defect.problem: The holding field says the Arizona Supreme Court applies the independent-source exception, but the opinion holds that the inevitable-discovery exception applies and does not decide other exceptions.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace with: Arizona Supreme Court held that, although warrantless DNA sequencing violated the Fourth Amendment, the DNA profile was admissible under the inevitable-discovery exception because the State would have inevitably obtained it through an independent, untainted statutory DNA-collection process after Mitcham's unrelated 2022 felony convictions.

reasons: Paragraph 37 states police would have inevitably obtained Mitcham's DNA profile from an independent, untainted source despite the warrantless search.
Paragraph 47 states the inevitable-discovery exception applies and says the court does not address whether other exclusionary-rule exceptions apply.
The independent-source discussion in paragraph 34 is explanatory background, not the dispositive applied exception.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep independent source only as background/root doctrine; make inevitable discovery the holding.
